entities.name: Jerónimo Valdés
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Jerónimo Valdés y de la Cuesta (1784–1855) was a prominent Spanish military officer and colonial administrator whose career spanned the tumultuous transition from the Age of Revolutions to the mid-19th century. Born in Viḷḷarín, Asturias, he distinguished himself as a steadfast royalist commander during the Spanish American Wars of Independence and later as a crucial general for the liberal cause in Spain's First Carlist War. Valdés's actions profoundly impacted the dissolution of Spain's colonial empire and the shaping of its nascent liberal state, positioning him as a significant figure in both Iberian and Latin American history.

Valdés commenced his military service in 1800, gaining combat experience in the Peninsular War against Napoleonic forces. By 1814, he was dispatched to Peru, where he rose through the ranks, eventually serving as a divisional commander under Viceroy José de la Serna. His most consequential engagement was the Battle of Ayacucho on December 9, 1824, where, despite a valiant defense, the royalist forces suffered a decisive defeat against the combined armies of Simón Bolívar and José de Sucre. This battle effectively sealed the independence of Peru and the end of Spanish dominion in mainland South America. After his return to Spain, Valdés became a leading general for the Cristino (liberal) forces during the First Carlist War (1833–1839), playing a vital role in campaigns against the Carlist insurgents. He later served as Captain-General of Cuba (1841–1843) and briefly as Minister of War in 1844.
